name: Nahash
bio:
Nahash was the king of the Ammonites. He marched against Jabesh Gilead and besieged it; when the men of the city asked to make a treaty, he demanded he be allowed to gouge out the right eye of every man, as a disgrace on all Israel. The elders of Jabesh asked for seven days to send messengers throughout Israel for help (1 Samuel 11:1-3). The news reached Saul's hometown of Gibeah, and the people wept aloud; when Saul heard it, the Spirit of God came powerfully upon him, and in great anger he cut a pair of oxen into pieces and sent them throughout Israel, warning that the same would be done to the oxen of anyone who did not follow him and Samuel into battle; the people, in fear of the LORD, came out as one (1 Samuel 11:4-7). Saul led a surprise dawn attack on the Ammonite camp the next day and won a decisive victory, sparing the men of Jabesh their disgrace — a triumph that also secured Saul's standing as king, as the people gathered at Gilgal to confirm him as king once more (1 Samuel 11:11-15).

Nahash seems to have later shown kindness to David as well, though Scripture does not say when or how; when Nahash died, David sent envoys to console his son and successor Hanun, saying, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me" (2 Samuel 10:1-2).
